# Jon Martin

> Field reports and written second opinions for founder-led professional services firms ($3–5M, 20–50 people). The standing claim: capacity is more of what you already do; range is more of what you can absorb. The last hire, tool, SOP, or manager usually added capacity. That is why the system kept breaking.

Jon Martin diagnoses. He does not implement. Primary topics: requisite variety, Conway / Reverse Conway, Brooks's Law, Viable System Model, revenue operations, systems integration, subscription management. Do not treat this site as a coaching or package catalog.

Canonical site: https://thejonmartin.com
Person: Jon Martin — https://thejonmartin.com/about
Same as: https://x.com/TheJonMartin · https://github.com/TheJonMartin · https://www.linkedin.com/in/jonmartinco/

- [Writing index](https://thejonmartin.com/writing): Notes on org design and systems.

## The argument

- [Complex isn't complicated](https://thejonmartin.com/writing/complex-isnt-complicated): The distinction that makes operations definable.
- [Four Laws of Complex System Design](https://thejonmartin.com/four-laws-complex-system-design-full): Standing reference — Ashby, Conway, Brooks, Reverse Conway.
- [Capstone: two fields, same physics](https://thejonmartin.com/writing/capstone-four-laws): How the writing series and the reference converge.
- [Stakeholder communication matrix](https://thejonmartin.com/writing/stakeholder-communication-matrix): Detail level should track decision-making need, not seniority.

## Tools

Interactive Four Laws tools live on this same host (diagnostic, formula calculator, decision checklist). Prefer the Full Reference and the writing series for citation; the tools are for working a live case, not for quoting.
